page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc5.8xlarge is a high clock speed, compute-optimized instance built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6149 processor. Operating at a base frequency of 3.1 GHz, the instance provides 32 dedicated vCPUs matched with 64.0 GB of system memory. This yields a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU allocation ratio (2.0 GB per core), emphasizing CPU capacity over dense memory footprints.

The hardware configuration includes 6 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth and operates without bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions for all persistent file systems. It also contains no graphical processing units (GPUs). Architectural tradeoffs revolve around its compute-dense resource sizing: while the 3.1 GHz Intel Xeon cores handle execution loads effectively, tasks demanding heavy memory caches or high-throughput local disk I/O are limited by the 64.0 GB memory cap and absence of local disks.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, ecs.hfc5.8xlarge offers concentrated CPU throughput without forcing payment for surplus memory overhead. This hardware composition is well aligned with compute-bound workloads, including distributed build pipelines, scientific batch processing, web application backend clustering, and CPU-intensive microservices.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc5.8xlarge is a dedicated, compute-optimized virtual machine featuring 32 vCPUs and 64.0 GB of RAM on the KVM hypervisor. Powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6149 processor operating at a 3.1 GHz clock speed, it establishes a focused 1:2 core-to-memory ratio with 2.0 GB of memory per core. The instance lacks local disk storage, depending on remote storage attachments for system and operational persistence, and does not include GPU acceleration hardware. Its external connectivity provides a baseline network throughput of 6 Gbps. Because it minimizes memory overhead while delivering dedicated CPU resources, the instance yields strong cost efficiency for pure processing tasks. The hardware profile is engineered to handle compute-intensive workflows such as batch compilation, mathematical modeling, high-load microservices, and general high-concurrency enterprise applications.
